difficultyRationale: Requires understanding why interfaces can contain private helper methods without adding them to the implementing class's inherited API.
prompt: Which statements about a `private` method declared in an interface are correct? Select all that apply.
explanation: A private interface method is available only within the body of that interface. It is not inherited by implementing classes and is not part of their externally callable API.

options.text: It can be used as an implementation helper by methods declared in the same interface.
options.explanation: Private interface methods exist to share implementation details inside the interface.

options.text: It is inherited as a private member by every implementing class.
options.explanation: Private interface methods are not inherited by implementing classes.

options.text: It is not part of the implementing class's callable inherited API.
options.explanation: Its accessibility is confined to the interface that declares it.

options.text: It is implicitly public because every interface method is public.
options.explanation: Interfaces may explicitly declare private methods; the blanket public rule does not apply to them.
